# Case 231: Return Value Units Changed

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Verdict** | ✅ **NO_CHANGE** |
| **Category** | No Change |
| **Classification** | Rule |
| **Platforms** | Linux |

| **Source files** | `catalog/cases/case231_return_value_units_changed/` |

**Category:** No Change (declared interface) | **Verdict:** ✅ NO_CHANGE — with a separate **behavioral break**

## Verdict and consumer impact

`net::session_timeout()` keeps its declaration, symbol and return type
(`long`). The documented unit is seconds; v2 returns milliseconds (30 →
30000). Every old consumer that follows the documentation now waits a
thousand times longer: a 30-second idle timeout becomes about 8 hours.

This is a **behavioral break**, not a source (API) or binary (ABI) break. As
a statement about the declared interface the verdict is `NO_CHANGE`, and that
stays true even with build data and sources (see below). The break is
recorded in `ground_truth.json` as `behavioral_break: true` with
`truth_scope: declared-interface`.

## Old/new diff

| v1.cpp | v2.cpp |
|--------|--------|
| `return 30;   // seconds` | `return 30000; // milliseconds` |

`v1.h` and `v2.h` are identical.

## abicheck command

```bash
g++ -shared -fPIC -g v1.cpp -o libv1.so
g++ -shared -fPIC -g v2.cpp -o libv2.so
abicheck compare libv1.so libv2.so --header old=v1.h --header new=v2.h
```

## Expected abicheck finding

```text
Compatibility: NO_CHANGE | Policy: strict_abi | Gate: ACCEPTED (exit 0)
Findings: 0 detected; 0 retained (0 gating, 0 non-gating); 0 review groups.
```

No `ChangeKind` is expected. The absence is the detection control; the
behavioral regression is recorded separately.

## Minimum evidence

`min_evidence: L2`. The public header AST is what establishes that the
*published* declaration is unchanged. Nothing deeper adds a fact: the case
was also compared at `--depth source` with `compile_commands.json` and both
source trees, and the result is still `NO_CHANGE`.

## Why abicheck reports nothing

abicheck's deterministic checks compare what the artifacts *declare*:
exported symbols, DWARF types and layout, header declarations, build flags,
and source-graph dependencies. All of those are identical here. The change
sits in an out-of-line function body, and its meaning (the unit of the returned number) exists only in
documentation. No static rule can tell a bug fix from a contract break in a
function body, so abicheck correctly does not guess. That is why
`ground_truth.json` records `truth_scope: declared-interface` and a separate
`behavioral_break: true`: **`NO_CHANGE` here does not mean "safe to ship".**
See [Behavioral & Semantic Compatibility](../../learn/behavioral-compatibility.md).

## Runtime failure demonstration

**Severity: an unchanged old consumer breaks at runtime; no static tool shows
it.**

```bash
g++ -shared -fPIC -g v1.cpp -o libv1.so
g++ -g app.cpp -L. -lv1 -Wl,-rpath,'$ORIGIN' -o app
./app            # session timeout = 30 s                       exit 0
g++ -shared -fPIC -g v2.cpp -o libv1.so   # swap in v2, no recompile
./app            # session timeout = 30000 s
                 # WRONG RESULT: timeout is no longer in seconds  exit 1
```

## Safe redesign

Put the unit in the type, so the compiler and abicheck can see it: return
`std::chrono::seconds` instead of `long`. Changing that later to
`std::chrono::milliseconds` changes the return type, which abicheck reports
(`func_return_changed`). Old consumers that stored the result in
`std::chrono::seconds` then fail to compile instead of silently computing a
wrong deadline: `milliseconds` does not convert implicitly to `seconds`, and
an explicit `duration_cast` makes the possible loss of precision visible. Both
are far better than a wrong value at runtime. Changing the return type of an
exported function in place is itself an ABI break, so do it through a new
function or in an ABI-major release.
With a plain number, add a new function (`session_timeout_ms()`) and keep the
old one in seconds.

## Cross-tool comparison

`abidiff` and ABICC also report no change: they compare the same symbols,
types and declarations. Catching this break needs a test that runs a consumer
against the new library (the `app.cpp` above is such a test).

---

## Ground-truth provenance

**Behavioral break:** Not a compatibility claim for the release. A static comparison at every evidence depth (binary, headers, build data, sources) sees the same declaration, the same symbol and the same layout, so NO_CHANGE is the truth only for the declared interface. The runtime witness breaks a valid old consumer: app.cpp treats the value as seconds, as documented, exits 0 against v1 and reports a timeout of 30000 s and exits 1 against v2. A unit lives in documentation, not in the type `long`, so no deterministic detector can see the change.
